content: Consolidating prop-drilled per-tab state into fewer composite components risks new coupling and re-render regressions: naive context consumption re-renders every consumer on any context value change (the same problem prop drilling had, in a new shape), and moving state 'up' to a shared composite parent without colocating it back down to where it's actually used creates fragile, hard-to-reason-about components. The fix pattern is state colocation (push state back down to the nearest common consumer, not up to a global shell) plus compound-component patterns for shared UI that need to read common state without every leaf re-rendering.
